LanguageData.ATC_Guide_Introduction: Choose a topic, then use the buttons below to open its page. This guide appears automatically once; reopen it from any page using User guide.
LanguageData.ATC_Guide_Content_GettingStarted:
CHOOSE HOW TO START
For ready-made translations, open Cloud sharing, choose a language, find your mod and download a suitable package. You do not need your own AI key to use cloud packages.
To translate yourself, start in Translation settings.

YOUR FIRST TRANSLATION
1. Confirm the target language. The provider, API URL and key must belong to the same service or plan.
2. For Custom_OpenAI, finish entering the URL and key, then explicitly refresh the model list or type a model ID.
3. Test the connection. Once successful, open Translation tasks and try one small mod first.
4. Check progress, pipeline logs and results before selecting more mods. AI translation may use paid service quota.
5. Check the text in game. Some screens may need reopening or a game restart to refresh.

Use Workbench to edit existing translations. Its Batch XML export/import feature handles several mods with an external editor or translation tool.
LanguageData.ATC_Guide_Content_Settings:
BASIC SETUP
In Translation settings, choose the target language and add an enabled translation API. Select the provider, enter its matching key and model, set a custom URL if needed, then test the connection.
Custom_OpenAI accepts OpenAI-compatible services. Leave the key empty only if the service does not require one. Refresh models manually after entering the settings; type an ID if the service has no model-list endpoint.
For MiMo Token Plan, use that plan’s URL and key from its console. Player2 uses its local protocol and Game Client ID; its application manages the model.

THINKING MODE — EACH API’S ADVANCED SETTINGS
Automatic (recommended): disable optional thinking for translation and retain it for policy review.
Prefer off: disable it where supported; mandatory-thinking models keep their lowest supported level or service default.
Enable thinking: enable it where supported; this may increase latency and usage. Unknown models or gateways retain service defaults. Read the status below the setting.
Translation and policy-review APIs save their choices independently.

ADDITIONAL TRANSLATION PREFERENCES
Open Advanced: translation preferences. For example: “Keep character names unchanged.” Up to 4000 characters; preview the full prompt, clear to restore defaults, then save.
Only new normal AI requests use these preferences. They do not change the policy Agent, DeepL, or existing translations automatically. Built-in output format, order, variables and tag safeguards remain.

POLICY REVIEW AND CONNECTION ERRORS
The optional policy Agent classifies ambiguous fields; it does not produce translations. Beginners can leave it off, then configure its separate API and call/token limits when needed.
Connection failures show a summary at the top left. View or copy diagnostics manually without developer mode. Check the URL, plan, key and model first. A missing model list alone does not prove translation cannot work.
LanguageData.ATC_Guide_Content_Workbench:
FIND AND EDIT TRANSLATIONS
In Workbench, search for a mod or text, select the mod, category and entry, then edit its translation. Use Save and apply when finished; text in an edit box is still a draft until saved.
Global search helps locate text across mods. Batch replacement can make terminology consistent. Preserve variables, format arguments and tags.

WORK ON MULTIPLE MODS
Batch XML export/import lets you select several mods, export their source text and import edits made externally. Full instructions follow below.
One-click package export outputs completed translation packages.
Wait for translation tasks to finish or stop them before batch editing the same content.
LanguageData.ATC_Guide_Content_Cloud:
DOWNLOAD EXISTING TRANSLATIONS
1. Open Cloud sharing and choose the cloud list’s target language.
2. Search for a mod name or ID; check translation type and version details.
3. Download a suitable package, follow the apply steps and inspect the text in game. Your own AI key is not required.

SHARE YOUR TRANSLATION
Finish and review the translation, select the mods or entries to upload, and enter a display name, accurate translation type and update notes. Complete the preview and confirmation steps.
Choose AI translation, player-refined or translation-team labels according to how the content was made. Check the language and selection before batch uploading.

WHEN CONTENT DOES NOT MATCH
Check the cloud language, mod and version first. Use Workbench to inspect and correct local text. Review it again before sharing so unfinished drafts are not uploaded as completed work.
